subject: Runtime access addendum — telemetry carveout review
messages:
From: Carlos Mendoza <carlos.mendoza@helixhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Health Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry carveout / runtime access addendum request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo Friday — Helix Health is excited by the latency and cost profile you showed. Legal ran a quick pass on the DPA and asked whether we can get an explicit addendum allowing a narrow runtime telemetry carveout for incident analysis. In short: they want Redwood to retain generated inference metadata (non-PHI) for 30 days and allow Helix to request a runtime-level audit trace if needed for a security incident.

Key asks from procurement/legal:
- Add a clause that runtime telemetry kept for up to 30 days, with access logs exported on request (Helix-approved audit only).
- Limit the export target to an S3 bucket owned by Helix (no model weights or raw input data).
- A subprocessors list for any tooling that touches telemetry (they flagged monitoring vendors).

Can you advise whether this is something Redwood can accept, and what product/security signoffs we need? Helix needs a counterproposal by Apr 19 to keep their procurement timeline. I attached their proposed redline.

Appreciate the quick help —
Carlos
Director, Procurement
Helix Health

Attachments: helix_redline_v1.docx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Telemetry carveout / runtime access addendum request

Folks — forwarding Helix's ask. Procurement wants a narrow runtime telemetry carveout: 30-day retention of non-PHI inference telemetry + Helix-requested audit exports to their S3. They explicitly ask for subprocessors list for any telemetry processors.

Can product/security review and propose the minimal redline we can accept + any operational constraints? Timelines: Helix needs a counter by 2026-04-19. I attached their redline and a short MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.

Quick context: this is for a Dedicated deployment with reserved capacity; they want the ability to request an audit trace for incidents. No model training rights requested.

Thanks — please reply with clear signoff language we can give procurement/legal.

- Rachel
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_redline_v1.docx, MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Telemetry carveout / runtime access addendum request

Thanks for the ping. Product questions before we draft language:

1) "Runtime telemetry" — can Helix define the exact fields they want retained? We should push to limit to non-identifying operational metrics: request ids, timestamps, input token counts, latencies, error traces. No user content or prompt text.
2) Export mechanics — do we want to support direct S3 exports to customer buckets, or require a Redwood-generated export delivered to Helix? The former has network/credentials implications.
3) Subprocessors — we have monitoring infra (TelemetryOps Inc) and an analytics vendor (Lookuply). We need to confirm whether either processes de-identified telemetry. If Helix requires vendor-level attestation we may need time.

I can draft a product-friendly clause that: limits fields, specifies 30-day retention, requires export via signed job to customer-owned S3 with RBAC approvals, and prohibits export of inputs/outputs. Leaving security to confirm controls and attestation language.

I'll attach a short draft by EOD.

- Priyom
Senior PM, Runtime

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Telemetry carveout / runtime access addendum request

Agree with Priyom. Security concerns and proposed redlines below — I've highlighted what we can accept vs. what needs compromise.

Acceptable (we can commit):
- 30-day retention for operational telemetry limited to de-identified fields (request_id, timestamp, latency_ms, error_code, model_variant).
- Export to customer S3 via signed export job initiated by Redwood with explicit Helix authorization; Redwood will require a written request + ticketing trace; exports will include metadata only, no raw inputs or model outputs.
- A subprocessors list shall be provided; any new telemetry subprocessor will require 30 days' notice and SOC2 attestation.

Needs negotiation / not acceptable as-is:
- Allowing Helix to "request a runtime-level audit trace" without a scoped definition — we need to define 'audit trace' precisely. Full KV cache or token stream cannot be shared.
- Direct remote access from customer to runtime internal logs or granting temporary admin credentials — not allowed.

Suggested compromise language for redline (short):
"Redwood may retain de-identified runtime telemetry (limited to request_id, timestamp, latency, error_code, model_variant) for up to thirty (30) days. Upon Customer's written request accompanied by a documented security incident reference, Redwood will produce a scoped telemetry export consisting solely of the retained metadata fields, delivered to a Customer-owned storage endpoint via a signed export job. The export will not include message payloads, prompts, model outputs, or KV cache contents. Redwood will provide a list of telemetry subprocessors and will not add new telemetry subprocessors without notifying Customer (30 days)."

Operational notes: we need an export job that records operator approval and a ticket id; product should add an audit-fence in Console for any export. Also confirm whether Dedicated customers can configure their own S3 endpoint or if we must proxy.

I'll mark this as security_signoff_needed: redline above is acceptable pending a brief operational playbook.

- Olga
Head of Product Security

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Telemetry carveout / runtime access addendum request

Operationally we can support the export flow Olga describes for Dedicated customers with two caveats: 1) we must ensure S3 endpoint connectivity is validated during onboarding (we can include this as an MIP in the mutual action plan), and 2) we need a throttled export job with size limits and an operator approval step to prevent misuse. I'll update the runbook and add the Console UI flag to create the signed export job.

Proposed next step: Rachel, if you want to give Helix the redline Olga drafted, I'll attach an operational bulleted checklist that procurement can sign off on. That checklist will include: connectivity test, RBAC approvers, max export size, and ticket id requirement.

If procurement pushes for anything beyond metadata (e.g., prompts or token stream), we will decline.

- Marcus
Director, Operations
